purpose: Reduce idle lockstep matcher work caused by row-boundary rounding, with unchanged greedy tokens and encoded output.
change: Choose the nearer row boundary around each equal-byte lane target, breaking ties upward, instead of always rounding upward. Seven added source lines and one removed line in encoding/lanes.rs. Batch size, lane counts, matchers, ISA dispatch, dictionary training and output reservation are unchanged. No input-name selector, parameter fitting, public API change, encoded-format change or new unsafe code.
correctness_proof: For sorted offsets, nearest-boundary selection with a consistent upward tie rule is monotonic in the target. The first boundary is zero and the final boundary is n, so the lanes partition all complete rows exactly once in row order. A row begins at the same byte offset, uses the same row-end window bound and the same greedy matcher. Its codes are independent of the lane that processes it. Joining the lanes therefore emits identical dictionaries, codes and row offsets, including duplicate offsets and empty lanes.

machine.isa: Existing runtime AVX-512F + POPCNT; no additional feature requirements

method.primary: Same seven prepared Vortex string-bench caches, same two budgets and training settings, full serialized writes and normal round-trip checks. Seven timed iterations after three warmups. Baseline/candidate order reversed on alternating columns. One process per column, existing mimalloc/current-thread runtime. Frozen baseline and final public Git dependency; release_debug, opt3, codegen-units1, LTO off, default x86-64 target. Exact baseline frame-pointer flags preserved. All accepted timings ran serially after all builds, tests, compatibility checks and binary hashes had completed.
method.native: Existing upstream tpch and clickbench full suites, default allocator/native bench profile, single frame-pointer flag as in the baseline, CPU8. Same TPC-H scale1.0/8MiB cap/threshold.2; full1m real URLs and200k reviews, plus10k FineWeb rows, threshold.5/seed42 for parquet corpora. URL and reviews baseline then candidate; TPC-H and FineWeb candidate then baseline. Actual sample counts are retained, including extra samples from minimum time.
method.interpretation: Throughput gain is old_ms/new_ms-1. FSST is a control, not a correction factor. The seven-column geometric means are small relative to control movement: call the general workloads roughly flat and claim the repeatable FineWeb gain. Decoder and training source are unchanged. No decoder gain is claimed.
method.inputs: The exact same existing seven caches as the preceding OnPair parser/fixup reports. No synthetic substitution or changed row selection.
method.scheduling: CPU2 became unsuitable: during the partial final series, unchanged FSST throughput was173.44MB/s in the candidate process versus213.40MB/s in the following baseline process on TPC-H. The entire CPU2 series was interrupted and excluded, including positive candidate cases. All partial raw logs are preserved. The entire seven-column suite was restarted on previously idle CPU8, rather than selecting individual favorable reruns. Process CPU/elapsed times were additionally collected; they include preparation and I/O outside timed writes and are diagnostic only.

work_model.method: Use exact baseline per-row code offsets to simulate the unchanged6-lane/256KiB batches and64-row probe. Sum the maximum of code count plus empty rows across lanes per batch. Omit the final exit probe; this is a work model, not a timing measurement or a hardware lower bound.
